title: State-weighted kinetic resolvent corridor
question: Does the kinetic nested commutator isolated by R-387 have a finite Gibbs-weighted corridor that is more stable than its raw operator norm, and what beta/resolvent restrictions are exposed by cutoff stress?

model.state_weight: N_beta(X)^2=Tr(rho_beta X^*X)+Tr(rho_beta X X^*) with rho_beta=Z^(-1)exp(-beta H)
model.operator_stress: ||K|| is tracked only as a finite cutoff stress control
model.corridor_candidate: beta>=1/2 and eta>=1 are tested as a fixed finite corridor whose late cutoff ratio is <=1 on the manifest grid
model.outside_stress: beta<1/2 or eta<1 is retained as an outside-corridor stress control
model.analytic_target: Use a state-weighted kinetic graph estimate at a fixed beta/eta only after proving an invariant core and source/volume bounds; do not infer beta or eta uniformity

adversarial_review.check: Raw operator norms and two-sided Gibbs seminorms are reported separately; a bounded weighted row is not relabelled an operator-norm bound.
The corridor is declared only for beta>=1/2 and eta>=1 on the sampled grid; lower beta or eta values are retained as outside stress controls.
Dimensions 3 through 24 are finite oscillator truncations; the operator growth is a route stress and not an asymptotic divergence theorem.
A momentum resolvent is used as a hostile seed; it breaks the coordinate commutator anchor and must exceed the mutation threshold.
No fixed-beta estimate is promoted to beta-independent common dynamics, shell summability, domain, Cook, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only the abstract Jacobi/commutator reduction; finite matrices, Gibbs traces and all cutoff or beta limits remain Python/open analysis.

qft_interface.closed: The finite stress distinguishes a strongly cutoff-growing operator norm from a narrower beta/eta-dependent Gibbs-weighted corridor for the isolated kinetic target.
qft_interface.open: The analytic state-weighted BKM/graph estimate, shell summability, beta/eta independence, source/volume/shape uniformity, invariant domain, Cook/common-alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary finite state-weighted interface only; no production-owner transfer or physical-sector conclusion is supplied.

boundary: Claim-nonbearing finite cutoff stress only. It proves no cutoff-uniform operator or Gibbs estimate, no beta/eta-independent topology, no shell summability, no domain or Cook/common-alpha convergence, no OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, no gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A result.
no_overclaim: The sampled corridor identifies a plausible state-weighted route and its parameter debt. It is neither a uniform estimate nor evidence that the raw operator norm can be discarded in the common algebra.
